verdict.rationale: Greptile's own CLI runs `greptile review` on the feature-branch diff in about 60 seconds, before a PR exists. Its `--agent` mode lets coding agents in tools like Cursor or Claude Code review their own code, so a local pre-push review is documented. The in-editor surface is the MCP integration, but it fetches comments on PRs that already exist, so pre-push review happens through the terminal or agent CLI rather than a native IDE extension. Missing for 10: native IDE plugin or extension for pre-push review, explicit confirmation that the CLI review matches the PR review, and hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I get the same review inside my IDE before I push, catching issues while the code is still in my editor

citations.quote: Run `greptile review`, get a review of the feature branch diff in 60 seconds.
Coding agents can use the greptile cli to review their own code
`greptile review --agent` outputs every greptile catch as raw text with a suggested fix for your agent to apply.
Instead of switching to GitHub or the Greptile dashboard, you can fetch comments, apply fixes, and manage coding patterns from your editor.
